target.title: fix(seo): escape JSON-LD script content to prevent breakout
target.body:
## Summary

`Layout.astro` embeds structured data with:

```astro
<script type="application/ld+json" set:html={JSON.stringify(item)} />
```

If any string field contains `</script>`, the HTML parser closes the script element early. That is a classic JSON-in-script breakout (used elsewhere as `\u003c` escaping).

## Change

```astro
JSON.stringify(item).replace(/</g, "\\u003c")
```

JSON.parse still yields the original characters; only the HTML parser is affected.

## Attack scenario

1. Structured data includes a title or description with `</script><script>alert(1)</script>`.
2. Without escaping, the first `</script>` ends the ld+json block and the following script runs in page origin.

## Validation

```js
// local proof
const item = {name: "</script><script>alert(1)</script>"};
const bad = JSON.stringify(item);   // includes literal </script>
const good = JSON.stringify(item).replace(/</g, "\\u003c"); // no literal </script>
JSON.parse(good); // still valid object with original name
```

## Real behavior proof

**Command:** `node -e '...'` (escape demo above)
**Input:** object whose name is `</script><script>alert(1)</script>`
**Output:** escaped string has no raw `</script>`; `JSON.parse` round-trips correctly
**Exit code:** 0
**Duration:** <1s
**Commit:** HEAD of this PR

## Related

- React / Next.js JSON-LD guidance: escape `<` as `\u003c` inside script tags
- Same-repo XSS series: #140, #142, #146
